question.stem:
In each independent case, a new partner brings a cash premium for goodwill, and the existing partners sacrifice part of their shares. Match each situation in List-I with its accounting treatment in List-II.

List-I
(A) The new partner pays the premium directly and privately to the existing partners.
(B) The premium is received through the firm and initially credited to Premium for Goodwill A/c.
(C) The premium is received through the firm and initially credited to the new partner’s capital account before distribution to the sacrificing partners.
(D) The premium has been credited to the existing partners’ capital accounts in their sacrificing ratio, and they retain the amount in the business.

List-II
(I) No entry is passed in the firm’s books.
(II) Bank A/c Dr. to Premium for Goodwill A/c; then Goodwill A/c Dr. to the sacrificing partners’ capital accounts individually.
(III) Bank A/c Dr. to the new partner’s capital account; then the new partner’s capital account Dr. to the sacrificing partners’ capital accounts individually.
(IV) No additional entry is passed for retaining the credited amounts in the business.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

cases.explanation: A premium paid directly and privately to the existing partners requires no entry in the firm’s books. When the premium is received through the firm, the entries depend on whether it is credited initially to Premium for Goodwill A/c or to the new partner’s capital account. If the credited amounts are retained in the business, no additional entry is passed.

5.5.1 When the new Partner brings goodwill in cash. The amount of premium brought in by the new partner is shared by the existing partners in their ratio of sacrifice. If this amount is paid to the old partners directly (privately) by the new partner, no entry is passed in the books of the firm. But, when the amount is paid through the firm, which is generally the case, the following journal entries are passed: (i) Bank A/c Dr. To Premium for Goodwill A/c (Amount brought by new partner as premium) (ii) Goodwill A/c Dr. To Sacrificing Partners Capital A/c (Individually)(Goodwill distributed among the existing partners’ in their sacrificing ratio). Alternatively, it is credited to the new partner’s capital account and then adjusted in favour of the existing partners in their sacrificing ratio. In that case the journal entries will be as follows: Reprint 2026-27
PAGE 18
Admission of a Partner 65 (i) Bank A/c Dr. To New Partner’s Capital A/c (Amount brought by new partner for his share of goodwill). (ii) New Partner’s Capital A/c Dr. To Sacrificing Partner’s Capital A/c’s (Individually) (Goodwill brought by new partners distributed among the existing partners in their sacrificing ratio) If the partners decide that the amount of premium for goodwill credited to their capital accounts should be retained in business, an additional entry is not passed. If, however, they decide to withdraw their amounts, (in full or in part) the following additional entry will be passed: Existing Partner’s Capital A/c (Individually) Dr.

2.5.4 Methods of Valuation of Goodwill Since goodwill is an intangible asset it is very difficult to accurately calculate its value. Various methods have been advocated for the valuation of goodwill of a partnership firm. Goodwill calculated by one method may differ from the goodwill Reprint 2026-27

Admission of a Partner 57 calculated by another method. Hence, the method by which goodwill is to be calculated, may be specifically decided between the existing partners and the incoming partner. The important methods of valuation of goodwill are as follows: 1. Average Profits Method 2. Super Profits Method 3. Capitalisation Method 2.5.4.1 Average Profits Method Under this method, the goodwill is valued at agreed number of ‘years’ purchase of the average profits of the past few years. It is based on the assumption that a new business will not be able to earn any profits during the first few years of its operations. Hence, the person who purchases a running business must pay in the form of goodwill a sum which is equal to the profits he is likely to receive for the first few years. The goodwill, therefore, should be calculated by multiplying the past average profits by the number of years during which the anticipated profits are expected to accrue. question.stem: A government records two receipts. The first is a tax receipt and the second is a non-tax receipt. Neither receipt leads to a claim on the government. How should these receipts be classified?
options: Both are revenue receipts: one is tax revenue and the other is non-tax revenue.
Only the tax receipt is a revenue receipt; the non-tax receipt is a capital receipt.
Only the non-tax receipt is a revenue receipt; the tax receipt is a capital receipt.
Neither receipt is a revenue receipt because neither leads to a claim on the government.

cases.explanation: A receipt that does not lead to a claim on the government is a revenue receipt. Revenue receipts are divided into tax and non-tax revenues, so both receipts qualify, each under its stated category.

All those receipts of the government which create liability or reduce financial assets are termed as capital receipts. cases.independent_check: Non-tax sale of a government asset creates no repayment claim but reduces assets and is a capital receipt. The stem does not exclude this counterexample; its universal revenue-receipt explanation is insufficient.
